item.title: November Supermoon lights up the night sky
item.description: The supermoon brightened the night sky on Tuesday.

item.title: Astronomers spot record-setting quasar in the early universe
item.description: Astronomers have now found the oldest-known quasar, one that formed so early in cosmic history that they are still trying to decipher how it happened.

item.title: Rare helmet orchids found by researchers in Bohol
item.description: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Region 7 found more than 700 Bohol Helmet Orchids after conducted fieldwork at Loboc Watershed Forest Reserve in Bohol.

item.title: NPC cautions public against sharing photos online amid deepfake threats
item.description: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) advised the public to be more cautious about the pictures they post online, as they could be used to create deepfakes.

item.title: China to launch Shenzhou-24 spaceship with first foreign astronaut
item.description: China will launch its Shenzhou-24 spaceship on Wednesday at 8:18 a.m. local time (0018 GMT) with a crew including a Pakistani national, who will be the first foreign astronaut to board China's space station.

item.title: Astronomers observe a huge puffy star merge with smaller companion
item.description: WASHINGTON - Astronomers have observed a large dying star, seven times more massive and 18,000 times brighter than the sun, engulfing a smaller companion in a stellar merger unlike any other previously witnessed.

item.title: Commuter develops app to track EDSA Carousel buses
item.description: A commuter has developed an app that allows passengers to track buses operating along the EDSA Carousel.

item.title: Brazilian students turn to burned fish bones as clean water filter
item.description: MANACAPURU, Brazil - A group of Brazilian high school students and their teacher have come up with a local solution for providing clean drinking water in remote areas of the Amazon: a filter made of charcoal produced by burning the bones of the region's giant pirarucu fish.

item.title: Scientists succeed in growing potatoes in simulated moon soil
item.description: Potatoes are one of the most important crops on Earth, a food that is a great source of starch, vitamins, minerals and fiber. They soon might be an important crop on the moon as well.

item.title: Elon Musk looking for SpaceX launch sites? Marcos says PH could look into it
item.description: SHENZHEN, China --- The Philippines intends to leverage on its geographical location by getting into business with Elon Musk amid his expansion of launch sites for SpaceX. President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. announced this to the Philippine media delegation in Shenzhen following his attendance in the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting.

item.title: NASA probe achieves light-day milestone and is 'not done yet'
item.description: WASHINGTON - NASA confirmed on Thursday its Voyager 1 probe has achieved an unprecedented distinction -- becoming the first spacecraft to travel beyond a light-day from Earth -- even as the aging probe runs low on power and experiences technical anomalies in a mission one official promised is "never going to end."

item.title: IAEA chief says planned US-Saudi nuclear deal 'very satisfactory' on inspections
item.description: The provisions in a planned US-Saudi nuclear deal for inspections in Saudi Arabia are "very satisfactory" even though they do not include the gold-standard Additional Protocol, the UN nuclear watchdog's chief said.

item.title: Governments warn Java flaw leaves computer systems open to hackers
item.description: Companies and organizations are urged to patch a critical flaw in the popular programming language Java that could allow hackers to access systems, the latest high-profile cyber incident.

item.title: Strain-specific Ebola jab trials to start in DR Congo next week -- WHO
item.description: GENEVA, Switzerland - Two potential vaccines against the deadly Ebola strain gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo are set to enter trials in the outbreak's epicenter next week, the WHO announced Tuesday.

item.title: Japan space probe changes target over engine trouble
item.description: TOKYO, Japan - A Japanese probe that returned precious asteroid dust to Earth six years ago has changed course in its extended mission, officials said Tuesday, citing issues in its ageing engines.
